sources.note: Nothing on stress; only note is onset clusters /pl, pʰl, bl, ml, pj, pʰj, bj, mj/ (after Hsiu/Xu). Chinese names 木达 / 母打; location Nanlianshan village community, Gasa township, Jinghong. References: Ethnologue 2015, Xu 1991, Hsiu 2018.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2018. Classifications of some lesser-known Lolo-Burmese languages. Blog post, sites.google.com/site/msealangs.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Muda of Xu (1991) is not the same as Muteun of Kato (2008). Muda appears to be an earlier split from Proto-Akha, and preserves Cl- consonant clusters like Jinuo, Kathu, and various Bisoid and Siloid languages.' Places Muda under Akoid. Names Xu (1991) as the only Muda data source.

sources.note: Nothing. Population 2,000 (2007), decreasing; Yunnan, Jinghong county, Nanpianshan district; Sino-Tibetan, Tibeto-Burman, Ngwi-Burmese, Ngwi, Southern; status 6b. No linguistic notes.

sources.note: The only published source with first-hand Muda (木达/母打) phonological data (per Hsiu 2018 and Wikipedia); comparative initials/rhymes/tones across Lolo-Burmese. Would at least give the Muda tone inventory and possibly a remark on syllable prominence; probably nothing on stress.
